doc.title: Dianne Reeves interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, October 13, 2001

title: Singing to America after September 11th
summary: She describes fear after 9/11, her grandmother's stories, and resolves to keep singing songs of strength.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: And I try to get creative in the classroom and probably we will wind up showing this video in my classroom. As a matter of fact several of my students were there to see you tonight and I played for them, to their sensibilities, in order to know how to appreciate your skill level, I played for them “Fascinating Rhythm.” I played “Send In the Clowns,” and I played “Lullaby of Birdland.” And so they kind of had some idea of what to expect. But if you could sing anytime, anyplace, about any subject, and you knew that the power of your voice would change, improve, enhance, inspire the sonic landscape, and anybody within the throw of your voice, how would you sing to America after September 11th?

I guess the way that I am now, from my heart. The interesting thing about what happened September 11th is it brought about, God, a profound sense of fear that I don’t think that I’ve ever felt before. But also it made me think about some of the stories that my grandmother used to tell me of the things that she went through. And I heard the stories but I didn’t feel that kind of fear. Didn’t know what she’d been through, being like just a couple of steps out of slavery. And one of the things that came out of it was forward thinking perseverance, and now allowing the fear to take you down. So in answer to your question I think I would just continue to sing songs about strength and forward movement and try to stay aware and clear and present. Because there are so many things right now that are happening that can seduce you into feeling like maybe — not that it’s worse than what it is, but losing your, I don’t know, your things that you believe in. Breaking down your belief systems. And you can’t let it do that. So I will continue to sing the kinds of songs the kinds of music that I’ve always sung, the kind of music that’s always gotten me through, and the kind of music that really has gotten me through this time.
Gotta make it through the night.
